findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added to its superclass UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) at line 160. There is no no-arg overload, so services module fails to compile and none of the PR can be built or tested. The call should pass context.getUser().

findings.title: Conditional passkeys are now disabled for unauthenticated (ID-less) login
findings.body: authenticate() previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when context.getUser() was null, which sets the WebAuthn challenge/RP attributes needed for discoverable-passkey (ID-less) login on the initial username/password page. The new code only calls it when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and that helper at lines 160-162 requires user != null. Consequently first-time/anonymous login pages get no challenge and no conditional-UI webauthn form, breaking passkey login for users not yet identified (existing tests such as webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey and passwordLoginWithExternalKey in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest expect the webauth form on the initial page). The helper should not require a non-null user; fillContextForm is already made safe for an identified user by WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning false.

findings.title: Error challenge also loses conditional passkeys for unauthenticated users
findings.body: challenge(context, error, field) previously refilled WebAuthn data when context.getUser() == null, i.e. after a failed initial login attempt. It now delegates to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which returns false for a null user. After an invalid username/password attempt by an unauthenticated user the re-rendered form therefore has no WebAuthn challenge/conditional-UI data, so the user cannot retry with a discoverable passkey from the error page, regressing the pre-existing behaviour that the authenticate() change also breaks.
